provenance: LLM-backend-derived (this session, no API key) + deterministic-checked — NOT a ship typology config. build_rec follows the cover×data matrix (build_rec_category); every indicator's flag is quote-grounded (verbatim) in the source md within the red-flag region (Phase 16). Coverage/data values are ILLUSTRATIVE (vision demo).

indicators.flag: Documentation associated with a customer’s oil shipping-related transactions is inconsistent with information contained in maritime database entries used for conducting due diligence
indicators.red_flag: Shipping docs inconsistent with maritime database — Iranian port call omitted
indicators.rationale: Shipping documents are captured in trade-finance data, but reconciling them against vessel port-call history requires a maritime database we hold only partially — build the doc-vs-maritime reconciliation after enriching the maritime feed.

indicators.flag: vessels that, according to maritime databases, have undergone recent or multiple name or flag changes, or transfer of ownership or operation to another person following OFAC’s designation of its owner or operator, but the designated owner or operator appears to maintain an interest in the vessel
indicators.red_flag: Vessel name/flag changes or post-OFAC ownership transfer with designated owner retaining interest
indicators.rationale: Name/flag-change and post-OFAC ownership-transfer history live in maritime vessel databases we hold only partially; the referenced-vessel data is in the trade docs — build after enriching vessel-history.

indicators.flag: vessels that claim an International Maritime Organization (IMO) number that, on examination of maritime databases, belong to a different vessel or to vessels that have previously been scrapped
indicators.red_flag: Spoofed IMO number — belongs to another or scrapped vessel
indicators.rationale: Validating a claimed IMO number against the registry of real / scrapped vessels needs maritime-database enrichment we hold only partially, paired with the trade-doc vessel reference we do hold — build after enrichment.

indicators.flag: Malaysian blend” oil, particularly if the vessel is bound for China by way of Southeast Asia and if maritime databases indicate that the vessel displayed AIS irregularities during its voyage or reveal evidence of a ship-to-ship transfer in proximity to Southeast Asia
indicators.red_flag: "Malaysian blend" oil reference with AIS irregularities / ship-to-ship transfer
indicators.rationale: Detecting 'Malaysian blend' relabeling plus AIS irregularities and ship-to-ship transfers requires vessel AIS-track data we do not source today — acquire AIS / voyage data before building.

indicators.flag: does business with counterparties that have ties to Iran or transports goods using vessels that have ties to Iran or that maritime databases indicate have made stops at Iranian ports
indicators.red_flag: Counterparties or vessels tied to Iran / Iranian-port stops
indicators.rationale: Counterparty ties to Iran are partially covered by sanctions / adverse-media screening, but confirming a vessel made Iranian-port stops needs maritime data we lack — monitor rather than alert until the data exists.

indicators.flag: vessels that have been previously linked to suspicious financial activities or that include documentation, such as bills of lading or shipping invoices, with no consignees, that appear to be falsified, or that omit key information, in an attempt to hide the Iranian nexus
indicators.red_flag: Vessel previously linked to suspicious activity, or falsified / no-consignee shipping docs concealing Iranian nexus
indicators.rationale: Bills of lading or shipping invoices that omit the consignee or key fields on an oil-related payment are checkable from structured trade-finance document fields in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: an oil-related payment is supported by bills of lading or shipping invoices that omit the consignee or other key fields, or reference a vessel on the suspicious-activity watchlist, consistent with concealing an Iranian nexus
build_logic.source: Trade-finance document fields (Gold); internal vessel watchlist
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → trade-finance sanctions review gate

indicators.flag: move through multiple exchange houses and/or trading companies, adding additional fees and costs as the transactions progress, where the fees, number of transactions, and pattern of transactions do not reflect standard and customary commercial practices
indicators.red_flag: Multi-hop exchange-house / trading-company layering with fee-stacking
indicators.rationale: Funds moving through multiple exchange houses / trading companies with fee-stacking and a non-commercial pattern is an uncovered layering shape computable from the transfer chain and counterparty types in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: funds move through multiple exchange houses or trading companies, accruing fees and hops that do not reflect standard commercial practice, consistent with shadow-banking layering
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → Iranian shadow-banking review gate

indicators.flag: An exchange house or trading company in a jurisdiction in close geographical proximity to Iran uses forged or falsified documents to conceal the identity of parties involved in transactions that will utilize regional banks’ correspondent banking relationships with U.S. financial institutions to access U.S. dollars.
indicators.red_flag: Iran-proximate exchange house using forged docs to reach U.S.-dollar correspondent access
indicators.rationale: Forged documents concealing party identity behind a regional bank's correspondent relationship hide the underlying party from us — the identity we would key on is not in our data; acquire correspondent / document-integrity data before building.

indicators.flag: receives wire transfers or deposits that do not contain any information about the source of funds, contain incomplete information about the source of funds, or do not match the customer’s line of business
indicators.red_flag: Missing / incomplete source-of-funds, or inflows inconsistent with line of business
indicators.rationale: Wire transfers or deposits with missing or incomplete source-of-funds information are already covered by established wire information-quality / Travel-Rule controls.

indicators.flag: A general trading company registered in a commercial free trade zone in the UAE with opaque ownership and whose trading counterparties are companies mostly located in Singapore and Hong Kong has bank accounts at multiple UAE financial institutions.
indicators.red_flag: UAE free-zone trading company, opaque ownership, multi-bank, SG/HK counterparties
indicators.rationale: UAE free-trade-zone registration and opaque ownership need corporate-registry enrichment we hold only partially, though the Singapore/Hong Kong counterparty geography and multi-bank pattern are in repo — build after enrichment.

indicators.flag: A company based in Hong Kong, that banks using a Chinese non-resident account, has little to no web presence, is co-located with numerous other similar companies, or is recently incorporated yet transmitting large payments with no adequate explanation for the source of funds, makes numerous payments in large figures to UAE general trading companies with no clear business purpose.
indicators.red_flag: Hong Kong company on Chinese non-resident account — large no-purpose payments to UAE traders
indicators.rationale: Payment flows to UAE trading companies are visible, but web-presence, co-location, incorporation-recency and Chinese-non-resident-account context need external enrichment we hold only partially — build after enrichment.

indicators.flag: transactions involving companies that originate with, or are directed to, entities that are general trading companies, suspected front companies, or companies that have a nexus with Iran
indicators.red_flag: Front-company / Iran-nexus counterparties — opaque ownership, obscure directors, co-located addresses
indicators.rationale: Front-company nexus is partially covered by sanctions / adverse-media screening; enhance with the opaque-ownership, obscure-name, and residential / co-located-address indicators.

indicators.flag: declares information about the nature of its business that is inconsistent with other available information, such as previous transaction history or associated transactional information, particularly if trade data indicates that they have a history of facilitating shipments to and from Iran and if they transact predominantly with technology companies or chemical suppliers
indicators.red_flag: Declared business inconsistent with Iran-shipment and tech/chemical-supplier transaction history
indicators.rationale: Declared-vs-actual business inconsistency is computable from transaction history, but corroborating an Iran-shipment trade history and tech/chemical-supplier nexus needs external trade-data enrichment we hold only partially — build after enrichment.

indicators.flag: transactions that are directed to companies that operate in unrelated businesses, and which do not seem to align with the customer due diligence (CDD) and other customer identification information collected during client onboarding and subsequent updates
indicators.rationale: A mismatch between CDD-declared business and counterparty sectors — e.g. receiving from commodities traders but sending to electronics suppliers — is computable from counterparty industry codes and stated business in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: an account's counterparties operate in businesses unrelated to its CDD-declared activity — for example receiving funds primarily from commodities traders while sending primarily to electronics suppliers — a procurement-layering profile
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → Iranian procurement review gate

indicators.flag: Multiple companies incorporated at roughly the same time share counterparties, addresses, owners, or name similarities and demonstrate similar transaction profiles
indicators.red_flag: Company cluster — shared addresses/owners/counterparties, same-time incorporation, recurring amounts
indicators.rationale: A cluster of companies sharing addresses, owners, or counterparties with near-identical recurring transaction profiles is computable from the entity-resolution graph and transaction features in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: multiple companies sharing addresses, owners, or counterparties and showing near-identical recurring transaction profiles form a cluster consistent with a coordinated front-company network
build_logic.source: KYC entity-resolution graph + core transaction features (Gold)
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → front-company network review gate

indicators.flag: A company based in the Middle East with links to Iran or that shows indications of being a front company receives payments primarily from petroleum companies and then makes payments primarily to electronics companies based in Hong Kong and China.
indicators.red_flag: Middle East company, Iran-linked or front-company indications — petroleum-in / HK-China-electronics-out
indicators.rationale: The petroleum-in / electronics-out sector-flow is computable, but classifying the Middle East counterparty as Iran-linked or a front company needs corporate-registry / adverse-media enrichment we hold only partially — build after enrichment.
